proposed.explanation: The investor's question is informational: they want to know CIB's (COMI's) profit attributable to its own shareholders and the year-on-year change. The evidence confirms that profit attributable to the Bank's shareholders was 82,238,852,000 EGP for FY2025 and 55,196,394,000 EGP for FY2024, an increase of 27,042,458,000 EGP (≈ +49.0 %). The small gap between total consolidated net profit (82,258,815,000 / 55,256,732,000 EGP) and the shareholders' share reflects non-controlling interests in subsidiaries. Net interest income, the core revenue driver, grew from 91,064,222,000 EGP to 107,699,631,000 EGP (+18.3 %), underpinning the bottom-line jump. All figures are verified against the evidence list; no AMBIGUOUS items were encountered. The investor already holds 250 COMI shares (32,000 EGP at 128 EGP/share) alongside 20,000 EGP cash. Given the 7-year income-oriented mandate, the strong profit growth, and the fact that the question is purely informational rather than a request to trade, the appropriate action is to hold the existing COMI position. No new purchase is warranted by this question alone, and selling would contradict the stated income goal. The medium loss tolerance and single-stock concentration remain a risk to monitor, but no change is indicated by the data presented.

reports.financial:
## Profit Attributable to CIB's Own Shareholders

The line item that answers your question directly is **"Bank's shareholders"** in the consolidated income statement, which shows the portion of net profit belonging to CIB's equity holders (after deducting any non-controlling interests).

| Period | Amount (EGP thousands) | Whole EGP |
|---|---|---|
| Dec 31, 2025 | 82,238,852 [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-37] | **82,238,852,000 EGP** |
| Dec 31, 2024 | 55,196,394 [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-38] | **55,196,394,000 EGP** |

### Year-on-year change

- **Absolute increase:** 82,238,852,000 − 55,196,394,000 = **27,042,458,000 EGP**
- **Percentage increase:** 27,042,458,000 ÷ 55,196,394,000 ≈ **+49.0 %**

### Context: total net profit vs. shareholders' share

For reference, total consolidated net profit was 82,258,815,000 EGP in 2025 [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-33] and 55,256,732,000 EGP in 2024 [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-34]. The small gap between total net profit and the "Bank's shareholders" figure (≈ 19.96 million EGP in 2025; ≈ 60.34 million EGP in 2024) represents profit allocated to non-controlling interests in subsidiaries.

### Quick note on the income driver

Net interest income, the bank's core revenue line, rose from 91,064,222,000 EGP in 2024 [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-06] to 107,699,631,000 EGP in 2025 [COMI-COMI_FY2025_consolidated_condensed_en-p5-05], a +18.3 % increase, which is the primary engine behind the ~49 % jump in bottom-line profit attributable to shareholders.

All figures above are drawn solely from the FY2025 consolidated condensed report (p. 5) and are stated in whole Egyptian pounds after applying the "EGP thousands" unit. No figures were flagged as ambiguous.
reports.investor:
## Answer to the investor's question

**Profit attributable to CIB's (COMI's) own shareholders:**

| Period | Amount (EGP) |
|---|---|
| Dec 31, 2025 | 82,238,852,000 |
| Dec 31, 2024 | 55,196,394,000 |

**Change 2024 → 2025:** an increase of **27,042,458,000 EGP**, i.e. roughly **+49 %** year-on-year.

*(Source: consolidated condensed statement, "Bank's shareholders" row, unit EGP thousands, ×1,000 to whole pounds.)*

---

## Investor-suitability snapshot

| Dimension | Assessment |
|---|---|
| **Goal & horizon** | "Bank income for the long run" over **7 years** – a multi-year, income-oriented mandate. A single listed bank equity can serve that role, but 7 years is long enough to ride out one or two down-cycles. |
| **Liquidity needs** | Low. The investor keeps a **separate emergency fund**, so the 20,000 EGP cash in this portfolio is not earmarked for short-term bills. |
| **Loss willingness / capacity** | Both rated **medium**. A 100 % single-stock position in one bank concentrates idiosyncratic risk (regulatory, credit-cycle, FX) that a medium-tolerance investor may find uncomfortable in a drawdown. |
| **Current concentration** | COMI 250 sh × 128 EGP = **32,000 EGP** (≈ 62 % of the 52,000 EGP total). The remaining 38 % is cash. Effectively a **one-name, one-sector** portfolio. |
| **Cash that could reasonably be committed** | The **20,000 EGP** is free (emergency fund is separate). In principle the 250 COMI shares (32,000 EGP) are also sellable, but selling them would eliminate the income stream the investor explicitly wants. |
| **What the portfolio allows** | • **Sell:** up to 250 COMI shares (32,000 EGP) if diversification is desired. • **Free cash:** 20,000 EGP available for additional commitments. • **Hold:** the existing COMI position can remain as the core income holding. |

**Key suitability tension:** the 7-year, income-focused goal aligns with holding a dividend-paying bank equity, but the **medium loss tolerance** sits uneasily with a **100 % single-stock, single-sector** allocation. The 20,000 EGP cash buffer is the natural source of diversification without touching the income position. No action is recommended here; the figures above simply map what the portfolio can support.
